nodes.label: Family
nodes.definition: Works framed for broad family-friendly audiences.

nodes.label: Josei
nodes.definition: Stories associated with media marketed primarily to adult women; not equivalent to romance.

nodes.label: Kodomo
nodes.definition: Animation intended primarily for children.

nodes.label: Seinen
nodes.definition: Stories associated with media marketed primarily to adult men; not equivalent to violent or psychologically dark material.

nodes.label: Shoujo
nodes.definition: Stories associated with media marketed primarily to adolescent girls; an intended audience rather than a plot genre.

nodes.label: Shounen
nodes.definition: Stories associated with magazines or source works marketed primarily to adolescent boys; an audience descriptor rather than an action genre.

nodes.label: Baihe
nodes.definition: Chinese female–female love/romance literary tradition.

nodes.label: Bara
nodes.definition: Male–male erotic or romantic works associated with gay male creator/audience traditions; not strictly a BL subtype.

nodes.label: Boys' Love
nodes.definition: Fiction centrally featuring romantic/affective relationships between male characters, commonly abbreviated BL.

nodes.label: CGDCT
nodes.definition: Cute Girls Doing Cute Things: ensemble-centered, typically low-stakes activity-focused stories.

nodes.label: Danmei
nodes.definition: Chinese male–male romance tradition, often linked to Chinese-source animation and novels.

nodes.label: Dark Fantasy
nodes.definition: Fantasy strongly using disturbing, bleak, horrific, or psychologically dark subject matter.

nodes.label: Gekiga (Plot)
nodes.definition: Mature and dramatic storytelling associated with the gekiga tradition, rather than an audience label.

nodes.label: Girls' Love
nodes.definition: Fiction centrally featuring romantic/affective relationships between female characters, commonly abbreviated GL or yuri.

nodes.label: Mecha
nodes.definition: Anime centered on giant robots or mechanized humanoid machines, piloted or autonomous.

nodes.label: Real Robot
nodes.definition: Mecha convention emphasizing grounded operational constraints, military deployment, and technical realism.

nodes.label: Romance
nodes.definition: Stories with central romantic attraction, relationships or courtship arcs.

nodes.label: Sekai-kei
nodes.definition: A mode linking intimate protagonists’ concerns and large-scale world crisis with little social/political mediation.

nodes.label: Slice of Life
nodes.definition: Stories emphasizing ordinary activities, routines, relationships and small-scale events.

nodes.label: Super Robot
nodes.definition: Mecha convention emphasizing singular heroic machines and extraordinary abilities.

nodes.label: Workplace
nodes.definition: Stories centrally concerned with work tasks, colleagues, and professional routines.

nodes.label: Wuxia
nodes.definition: Chinese martial-heroic tradition organized around itinerant martial artists, sects, codes of honor, and combat.

nodes.label: Xianxia
nodes.definition: Chinese cultivation-immortal fantasy tradition featuring progression through spiritual training, supernatural powers and mythic realms.

nodes.label: Body Sharing/Body Swapping/Reincarnation
nodes.definition: Broad umbrella for several distinct bodily identity or rebirth premises; use specific subordinate tags when possible.

nodes.label: Ecchi
nodes.definition: Erotically suggestive or fan-service-oriented content without a requirement of explicit sexual depiction.

nodes.label: Hentai
nodes.definition: Explicit pornographic animated content classification; adult-only and excluded from ordinary browse by default.

nodes.label: Military
nodes.definition: Subject matter centered on armed forces, hierarchy, warfare preparedness or military life.

nodes.label: Sports
nodes.definition: Athletics and competition as a central narrative subject.

nodes.label: War
nodes.definition: Organized armed conflict as a substantive story theme.

nodes.label: Comedy
nodes.definition: Stories centered on humor, jokes, playful conflicts, or comic setups.

nodes.label: Horror
nodes.definition: Stories designed around fear, dread, uncanny threat, and disturbing content.

nodes.label: Iyashikei
nodes.definition: Healing or restorative storytelling emphasizing calm atmosphere and everyday experience.

nodes.label: Noir
nodes.definition: Crime and drama conventions characterized by moral ambiguity, fatalism, alienation, and hard-boiled presentation.

nodes.label: Psychological
nodes.definition: Stories where characters’ cognition, perception, trauma or mental life are central to the dramatic experience.

nodes.label: Thriller
nodes.definition: Stories centered on danger, uncertainty, high-stakes tension and suspense.

nodes.label: Magic Idol Singers
nodes.definition: An anime character/trope crossover combining magical-girl conventions with idol performance or singing.

nodes.label: Mahou Shoujo
nodes.definition: Magical-girl convention centered on magically empowered young heroines, often including transformation sequences.

nodes.label: Villainess
nodes.definition: Stories featuring a female character positioned as a villainess in a romance/game or fantasy narrative, often trying to change her fate.

nodes.label: Cyberpunk
nodes.definition: Science-fiction worldbuilding featuring pervasive computing or cybernetics, frequently against social inequality or institutional control.

nodes.label: Fantasy
nodes.definition: Works featuring impossible or magical worldbuilding, supernatural systems, or fantastical premises.

nodes.label: Isekai
nodes.definition: Stories in which characters travel to, are summoned into, are trapped in or are reborn into another world or reality.

nodes.label: Magic School
nodes.definition: Stories centered on an institution where characters formally study magical arts.

nodes.label: Post-apocalyptic
nodes.definition: Set after a destructive world-shaping catastrophe, whether or not society is oppressive or dystopian.

nodes.label: School Club
nodes.definition: Stories substantially organized around membership and activity in an extracurricular school club.

nodes.label: Science Fantasy
nodes.definition: Narrative setting deliberately blending technological/science-fiction conventions and fantastical or magical ones.

nodes.label: Science Fiction
nodes.definition: Speculative works built around science, technology, futuristic conditions or scientific extrapolation.

nodes.label: Space Opera
nodes.definition: Large-scale, space-set speculative adventure emphasizing sweeping conflict and interpersonal drama.

nodes.label: Monster-of-the-week
nodes.definition: Mostly episodic episodes each featuring a separate antagonist or monster.

nodes.label: Reincarnation
nodes.definition: A character is reborn into a new body or life, without necessarily transferring between worlds.

nodes.label: Reverse Isekai
nodes.definition: Otherworldly characters come to Earth or another ordinary home world, reversing the common isekai direction.

nodes.label: Trapped in a Video Game
nodes.definition: Plot where characters are unable to leave a videogame-like environment.

nodes.label: CG Animation
nodes.definition: Animation produced using three-dimensional or computer-rendered techniques rather than primarily hand-drawn cel-based methods.

nodes.label: Gekiga (Style)
nodes.definition: Graphic aesthetic influenced by the realistic or dramatic linework of gekiga.

nodes.label: ONA
nodes.definition: Original Net Animation: animation initially released online.

nodes.label: OVA
nodes.definition: Original Video Animation: first-distributed primarily through home video rather than first-run television or theatrical release.
